title: Hunting for parts
situation: You are {{Markus}}. It is night, and rain is falling on the docks. {{Jericho}} is running out of everything; its androids are shutting down for lack of spare parts and blue blood, and you have come to steal some. You climb onto the dock with {{North}}, {{Simon}} and {{Josh}}. {{Josh}}: “This is crazy... If they catch us, we’re dead...” {{Simon}}: “What do we do now?” You: “We need to find the {{CyberLife}} warehouse. That’s where they keep the spare parts and the blue blood.” {{North}}: “Follow me!” You follow her between the rows of shipping containers while dock workers load cargo nearby. {{Simon}}: “Humans... Don’t let them see us...” Two guards are standing at the far end of a row. You edge toward them and are almost seen before you rejoin the group. {{North}}: “Watch out!” You climb onto the containers and make your way across them toward the {{CyberLife}} yard. {{Simon}}: “There are surveillance drones everywhere... We need to be careful...”
facts: You, {{North}}, {{Simon}} and {{Josh}} have slipped into the docks at night to steal spare parts and blue blood for {{Jericho}} from the {{CyberLife}} warehouse. {{Josh}} said that if you are caught, you are dead.

outcomes.0: The group moves on across the container tops.

adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint HUNTING FOR PARTS and its scripted line CLIMB ONTO DOCK, FOLLOW NORTH, ALMOST SPOTTED, CLIMB ON CONTAINERS and PROGRESS TOWARD CYBERLIFE, narrated as one event. The lines are the game’s (transcript and string table: “This is crazy... If they catch us, we’re dead...”, “We need to find the CyberLife warehouse…”, “Follow me!”, “Humans... Don’t let them see us...”, “Watch out!”, “There are surveillance drones everywhere...”). ALMOST SPOTTED is narrated as always happening. PowerPyx says Markus has to walk toward the two guards to light the node, and the chart has a stub line suggesting it can be skipped (research note §8.6); it changes nothing either way. Left out: {{North}} calling out if {{Markus}} lags behind (a timer with no effect). The reason for the raid (Time to Decide: {{Jericho}} short of parts) is restated in one clause because chapter 16 has no scenes of its own yet. No stat change; the template has none here.

title: The crane
situation: You are {{Markus}}, on top of the containers. Ahead, a crane is swinging a crate across the gap toward the warehouse. {{North}} and {{Josh}} have jumped onto it. {{North}}: “{{Markus}}, climb up here!” {{Simon}} has gone the other way and is jumping from container to container. The crate will not wait long.

options.text: Jump onto the crate on the crane with {{North}} and {{Josh}}.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} leaps onto the swinging crate beside {{North}} and {{Josh}}. {{Josh}}: “Nice…” The crane carries them across, and the group gathers again on the far side. {{North}}: “The warehouse is up ahead. We’re almost there.”

options.text: Go around with {{Simon}}, jumping across the containers.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I’ll go around…” {{North}}: “Where the hell are you going?” {{Simon}}: “{{Markus}}, that way!” The crate rises out of reach and {{Markus}} follows {{Simon}} across the containers; the group gathers again on the far side. {{North}}: “The warehouse is up ahead. We’re almost there.”

adaptationNote: The chart’s choice pair FOLLOW NORTH (the crane) or FOLLOW SIMON (over the containers), both rejoining at DRONE BLOCKS PATH. In the game it is a movement choice, not a button prompt; the template records it only as the condition “Follow Simon”. Lines from the transcript and string table (“Markus, climb up here!”, “Nice…”, “I’ll go around…”, “Where the hell are you going?”, “Markus, that way!”, “The warehouse is up ahead…”). In the game, waiting too long also means the crate rises out of reach (wiki Notes). No stat change: neither the template nor the wiki gives one.

title: The drone
situation: You are {{Markus}}, crouched with the others at the edge of the {{CyberLife}} yard. A security drone hovers in front of the warehouse, blocking the way in. {{Simon}}: “{{CyberLife}} warehouses… They have everything we’re looking for…” {{North}}: “First, we have to get rid of that drone…” You: “Leave it to me.” You work out a climbing route up the stacked crates. From the top you could jump onto the drone and bring it down.

options.text: Climb up the crates and jump onto the drone to bring it down.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} lands on the drone and smashes it to the ground, unharmed. {{Simon}}: “You okay?” {{Markus}}: “Yeah… Yeah, I’m fine.” {{North}}: “Good job, {{Markus}}…”

outcomes.damaged: {{Markus}} brings the drone down, but he hits the ground hard with it and is damaged. {{Simon}}: “{{Markus}}… You alright?” {{Markus}}: “Nothing I can’t handle…” {{North}}: “Nice work…”

adaptationNote: The chart’s DRONE BLOCKS PATH and NEUTRALIZE DRONE, then the quick-time pair MARKUS UNHARMED (success) or MARKUS DAMAGED (failure). The game has no choice here: {{Markus}} always takes the drone down, and the button inputs decide whether he is hurt. So this is a single action with a risk roll. No source gives a probability; the value is the operator’s to confirm, like every risk in the benchmark. Arrows from the template: “Succeed Attacking Drone” North, Simon and Josh small up (+1 each); “Fail Attacking Drone” the same three small down (−1 each). The wiki and PowerPyx also list a Jericho arrow here, but the template has none, so none is applied (research note §10.3 item 1). The damage has no later effect: {{Markus}} “cannot be killed before Freedom March” (Markus page).

title: Reach {{CyberLife}}
situation: You are {{Markus}}. The drone is down. The four of you get into the {{CyberLife}} warehouse, a hall of stacked crates under harsh lights. You pry the first crate open and find biocomponents and blue blood. {{Simon}}: “Quick, open the other crates and fill your bags. Take as much as you can!”
facts: The {{CyberLife}} warehouse crates hold biocomponents and blue blood, and you have started filling your bags.

outcomes.0: The group spreads out among the crates.

adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint REACH CYBERLIFE and GATHER SPARE PARTS, narrated as one event. Simon’s line is the game’s. No stat change.

title: The security android
situation: You are {{Markus}}, bent over an open crate and filling your bag. A security android in a {{CyberLife}} uniform steps around the crates and stops in front of you: “You are trespassing on private property. Your presence constitutes a Level 2 infraction. I will notify security.” Before he can, a human guard calls from across the warehouse, coming closer: “{{John}}! {{John}}! Goddamn machine... where is it this time?” The others are crouched behind the crates. The guard has not seen any of you yet.

options.text: KILL GUARD: attack the human guard before he can raise the alarm.
options.outcome: The guard rounds the crates: “What are you doing? I told you to-” {{Markus}} is on him before he can finish and kills him. {{Josh}} stares at the body in horror. The security android, {{John}}, stands frozen. Seeing a human killed in front of him has broken something in his programming, and he calls no one.

options.text: GRAB AND HIDE: seize the security android and pull him into cover with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} grabs the android and drags him down behind the crates: “I need your help…” Something in the android gives way. He stops resisting and stays silent; whatever held him to his orders has broken. Footsteps come closer. The guard: “{{John}}?”

options.text: RUN AWAY: get everyone out before the guard arrives.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Let’s get outta here!” The group runs, bags half empty. Behind them the guard shouts at the android: “What are you waiting for? Hit the fucking alarm!” Sirens start to wail across the docks.

options.text: HIDE: stay hidden behind the crates and hope the guard walks past.
options.outcome: The guard reaches the android: “What the hell you doing? I told you to wait for me!” The android answers: “There are four androids hiding behind these crates.” The guard: “What are you waiting for? Hit the fucking alarm!” Sirens wail across the docks and the group runs, bags half empty.

adaptationNote: The chart’s SECURITY ANDROID APPEARS and its four-way group ATTACK, GRAB ANDROID AND HIDE, RUN AWAY and HIDE, in the chart’s order. The button labels are the template’s (“Kill Guard”, “Grab and Hide”, “Run away”, “HIDE”). The scene’s own prompt keys read KILL HUMAN GUARD, SEIZE ANDROID, FLEE and HIDE; which wording is on screen is open (research note §10.3 item 2). Lines are the game’s. Arrows from the template: Kill Guard Josh large down (−2); Run away North small down twice (−2) and Jericho, Josh and Simon small down (−1 each). HIDE and Grab and Hide have none. ATTACK gives MARKUS SPILLS BLOOD and JOHN BECOMES DEVIANT (wiki John: “If Markus kills the guard, John will deviate on his own due to the emotional shock”). GRAB gives JOHN BECOMES DEVIANT and GUARD SEARCHES FOR SECURITY ANDROID. RUN AWAY and HIDE both lead to ALARM SOUNDS and the fence: John raises the alarm and the group flees before the bags are full, so the chapter ends in the Jericho block “Ran away when the guard arrived”. PowerPyx says HIDE “ends in the team running away and ending the mission early”; whether HIDE carries that block is open (§8.7). RUN AWAY is offered because the benchmark models Experienced difficulty; on Casual it is absent (PowerPyx comments). None of the four can fail. The previous version gave grabbing and attacking a 15% and 10% failure, which no source supports. The game’s time-out “[do nothing]” is not offered (§8.8).

title: The guard searches
situation: You are {{Markus}}, crouched behind the crates with the others. You are holding the security android, {{John}}, who has gone quiet in your grip. The human guard is right on the other side, sweeping the crates with his flashlight: “{{John}}?” He has not seen you yet.

options.text: ATTACK: kill the human guard.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} lets go of {{John}}, lunges from cover and kills the guard. {{John}} stands by and does nothing. {{Josh}} stares at the body in horror. {{Simon}}: “Let’s finish up and get out of here!” {{Josh}}: “Try to find some blue blood! We still don’t have enough!”

options.text: RELEASE: let {{John}} go and trust him to cover for you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} lets go. {{John}} steps out in front of the crates, shielding them from sight. The guard: “There you are. What the hell are you doing?” {{John}}: “I was inspecting the platform. Everything is in order.” The guard: “Good - then I’m going back to the control station. I’m soaked. Take the drone to maintenance and make a report.” {{John}}: “Understood.” The guard leaves. {{Simon}}: “Let’s finish up and get out of here!” {{Josh}}: “Try to find some blue blood! We still don’t have enough!”

options.text: HOLD: keep still and keep holding {{John}}.
options.outcome: Nobody moves. The guard’s flashlight passes over the crates and misses them. “First the drone, now this… Just my luck…” He walks away. {{Simon}}: “Let’s finish up and get out of here!” {{Josh}}: “Try to find some blue blood! We still don’t have enough!”

adaptationNote: The chart’s GUARD SEARCHES FOR SECURITY ANDROID, after GRAB ANDROID AND HIDE only, with its group ATTACK, RELEASE and HOLD POSITION in the chart’s order. The button labels are the template’s (“ATTACK”, “Release”, “Hold”). The scene’s prompt keys read KILL HUMAN GUARD, RELEASE ANDROID and DON’T MOVE. ATTACK leads to MARKUS SPILLS BLOOD; RELEASE and HOLD lead to HUMAN GUARD LEAVES. Lines are the game’s, and the wiki John page describes {{John}} shielding the crates on RELEASE and standing by on ATTACK. Arrows: ATTACK Josh large down (−2), from the template; RELEASE and HOLD have none. None of the three can fail, since the chart has no alarm edge out of this group. Simon’s and Josh’s closing lines play after the encounter (string table, X0602M.WAREHOUSE.SURPRISE).

title: Resume the search
situation: You are {{Markus}}, back at the crates with your bag half full. The security android, {{John}}, no longer bound by his orders, stands aside and lets the group work.

situationWhen.text: The guard’s body lies where he fell.
The human guard has gone back to his station.
Up on a platform at the end of the row stands a much bigger crate than the others.

options.text: Check the bigger crate up on the platform.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} climbs up onto the platform and opens the big crate.

options.text: Leave it, and finish filling your bag from the crates already open.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} leaves the big crate alone and fills his bag from the open crates.

adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint RESUME SEARCH (after MARKUS SPILLS BLOOD or HUMAN GUARD LEAVES). It has two lines out: one to FIND CRATE OF ANDROIDS and one straight to JOHN WANTS TO JOIN, and the wiki says the crate “can jump directly to John Wants to Join”. The game’s objective is CHECK THE BIGGER CRATE. The skip is offered as a choice because the chart draws that edge. The game’s unused “OVERLOOK CRATE OF ANDROIDS” node is not built. The wiki says {{John}} “will stand aside and let the group steal freely”. No stat change.

title: The crate of androids
situation: You are {{Markus}}, on the platform. Inside the big crate stand three androids, new, inert, waiting to be shipped. You look at them: “Why aren’t you like us? Don’t you wanna be free?” You could wake them with a touch, as you woke yourself.

options.text: FREE THEM: touch them and wake them.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} lays his hand on the first android, then the next. One by one their eyes come alive. Three androids stand awake in the crate, free.

options.text: CLOSE AGAIN: close the crate and leave them as they are.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} closes the crate on the three still androids.

adaptationNote: The chart’s FIND CRATE OF ANDROIDS and its pair FREE ANDROIDS or LEAVE ANDROIDS. The button labels are the template’s (FREE THEM, CLOSE AGAIN). Markus’s line is the game’s. The wiki location page says there are three androids. The Markus page calls this the first on-screen use of his converting touch; how he woke himself (Broken) is the benchmark’s framing. Arrows from the template: FREE THEM North, Simon and Josh small up (+1 each). The wiki and PowerPyx add Jericho up, but the template has none, so none is applied (§10.3 item 1). CLOSE AGAIN has none. Freeing does not bring the androids along: that is decided at ACCEPT (“They come with us.”). The previous version brought them along here.

title: {{John}} wants to join
situation: You are {{Markus}}. Your bags are as full as you can carry. {{Simon}}: “That’s all we can carry. Let’s go!” The security android, {{John}}, steps in front of you: “Take me with you.” {{North}}: “He’s on their side. We can’t trust him.” {{Josh}}: “He took a risk for us. We can’t just leave him here.”

situationWhen.text: {{Simon}}, looking at the three androids you woke: “We can’t bring them back with us. It’s too dangerous!”
{{Simon}}: “We can’t bring him back. It’s too dangerous!”

options.text: ACCEPT: take {{John}} with you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “He comes with us.” {{John}} joins the group.

options.text: REFUSE: tell {{John}} he cannot come.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “I’m sorry. You can’t come with us.” {{John}}: “I helped you… It’s not fair. I helped you and now you’re just gonna leave without me? You’re no better than humans. YOU’RE NO BETTER THAN HUMANS!” He hits the alarm. {{North}}: “He triggered the alarm! RUN!”

outcomes.quartet: {{Markus}}: “They come with us.” {{John}} and the three androids from the crate join the group.

adaptationNote: The chart’s JOHN WANTS TO JOIN and its pair ACCEPT or REFUSE; the button labels are the game’s. Lines are the game’s, and Simon’s line and Markus’s answer change if the crate androids were woken (template condition “Awoke androids”, wiki Notes). Arrows from the template: ACCEPT North small down, Simon small down, Josh small up. The wiki’s Jericho up on “Taking other androids with them” is not in the template and is not applied (§10.3 item 1). REFUSE has none. REFUSE leads to ALARM SOUNDS and the fence with full bags (the chapter’s “full bags” ending if {{Markus}} makes it), and {{John}} stays behind. ACCEPT makes {{John}} a companion: he leads to JOHN MENTIONS KEY. The previous version missed North’s arrow.

title: The truck key
situation: You are {{Markus}}, with your group and {{John}}. {{John}}: “I know where you can find more spare parts.” {{Simon}}: “What do you mean?” {{John}}: “The trucks. They’re full of biocomponents. They run on auto pilot, but they can be driven manually with a key.” You: “Where is this key?” {{John}}: “Down there, in the control station. There are two human guards. You’ll have to get the key without being noticed.” {{Simon}}: “This is suicide, {{Markus}}. Our bags are full. We got what we came for, let’s go before they catch us.” {{North}}: “This is a truck full of spare parts… There’d be enough for all of us… We can’t pass this up!” {{Josh}}: “And if we get killed, our people will have nothing. We can’t take that chance. It’s too risky!”

options.text: GET THE KEY: go down to the control station alone for the key.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “Wait here. If I’m not back in ten minutes, go without me.” {{Josh}}: “{{Markus}}…” {{North}}: “I’m coming with you.” {{Markus}}: “No, I’m going alone. It’s not worth it for both of us to risk losing our lives.”

options.text: LEAVE: go now with what you have.
options.outcome: {{Markus}}: “It’s not worth the risk. We have what we need.” {{John}}: “We can go over the fence. It’s the quickest way out.” {{Markus}}: “Ok then, let’s go!”

adaptationNote: The chart’s JOHN MENTIONS KEY and its pair ACCEPT or REFUSE. The button labels are the game’s (GET THE KEY, LEAVE). Lines are the game’s. Arrows from the template: GET THE KEY North small up, Simon small up, Josh small down; LEAVE North small down, Josh small up. LEAVE goes straight to RUN TO FENCE with no alarm. The previous version merged this prompt with the control-room methods into one three-way scene and never applied GET THE KEY’s arrows.

title: The control room
situation: You are {{Markus}}, alone, in the rain by the guard station at the gate. You climb in through a window into a dark back room. Through the doorway you can see two human guards at their desks. The truck key lies on the console beside them. Outside, the guard dogs will not stop barking. One guard: “Goddamn dogs… What the fuck are they barking at?..” The other: “Could be the weather… They don’t like storms…” “Yeah, I was going to take my kids camping this weekend. So much for that.” “Is {{Mike}} still in Zone 4?” “Looks like it… He should be done already…” “Better off in here than out patrolling in that.” Around you: a gun in a case on the wall, a screwdriver by the server cabinet, and, outside the window, a stack of oil drums.
facts: The truck key is on the console in the guard station, where two human guards sit talking. Guard dogs are kept outside.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} weighs how to get the key.

adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint CONTROL ROOM and its actions ENTER ROOM and FIND KEY (“THE KEY IS HERE”), narrated as one event. The guard chatter is the game’s (string table, X0602M.CONTROLROOM.CHITCHAT); {{Mike}} is the human guard from the warehouse. The three objects are the game’s interaction points: TAKE GUN (the case), ATTRACT GUARD (the barrel) and SHORT CIRCUIT (the screwdriver). PowerPyx says {{Markus}} goes in and out of the window. Exactly where each object sits is simplified. No stat change.

title: Two guards and a key
situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the dark back room of the guard station. Two human guards sit between you and the truck key on the console. You have to get the key without being seen, or deal with the guards.

options.text: TAKE GUN: take the gun from its case and hold the guards at gunpoint.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} steps in with the gun leveled. The guards throw their guns on the floor. As he reaches for the key, one of them kicks his chair into {{Markus}} and both guards jump him. {{Markus}} fights them off and knocks them both out cold. He takes the key and runs back to the others. {{North}}: “Did you get it? Nice.” {{Markus}}: “Hurry, get in!”

options.text: ATTRACT GUARD: go back out of the window and knock over the oil drums to draw the guards outside.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} knocks the drums over in the yard. “Fuck, what was that?” “The drums fell down…” While the guards go out into the rain to look, {{Markus}} slips back in through the window, takes the key from the console and is out again before they return. “I’m soaking wet here… all that for a fucking drum…” He runs back to the others. {{North}}: “Did you get it? Nice.” {{Markus}}: “Hurry, get in!”

options.text: SHORT CIRCUIT: jam the screwdriver into the server to black out the station.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} jams the screwdriver into the server and the station goes dark. “Shit, what’s going on?” “Lights are still on outside. Must be the fuse box…” While the guards hunt for the fuses by flashlight, {{Markus}} takes the key from the console and slips out. Behind him: “Somebody jammed the circuit with a screwdriver!” He runs back to the others. {{North}}: “Did you get it? Nice.” {{Markus}}: “Hurry, get in!”

options.text: Walk straight in and take the key from under their noses.

outcomes.kill: {{Markus}} steps in with the gun leveled. The guards throw their guns on the floor. As he reaches for the key, one of them kicks his chair into {{Markus}} and both guards jump him. {{Markus}} chokes one of them until he goes limp. The other gets a gun on him, and {{Markus}} shoves the limp guard into him and shoots him dead. With blood on his hand, he takes the key and runs back to the others. {{North}}: “Did you get it? Nice.” {{Markus}}: “Hurry, get in!”
outcomes.alarm: {{Markus}} steps in with the gun leveled. The guards throw their guns on the floor. As he reaches for the key, one of them kicks his chair into {{Markus}} and both guards jump him. They wrestle him down, and one of them gets to the alarm: “Motherfucker! Hit the alarm! Hurry!” Sirens wail across the docks. {{Markus}} breaks free and runs, without the key.
outcomes.lureSeen: {{Markus}} knocks the drums over in the yard. “Fuck, what was that?” “The drums fell down…” The guards come out into the rain, and one of them turns at the wrong moment: “There!” “Don’t move, asshole!” “Holy shit! Hit the alarm, hurry!” Sirens wail across the docks. {{Markus}} runs, without the key.
outcomes.blackoutSeen: {{Markus}} jams the screwdriver into the server and the station goes dark. “Shit, what’s going on?” “Lights are still on outside. Must be the fuse box…” Then: “Somebody jammed the circuit with a screwdriver! There must be someone in here… Show yourself!” The flashlight finds {{Markus}}. “There!” “Don’t move, asshole!” “Holy shit! Hit the alarm, hurry!” Sirens wail across the docks. {{Markus}} runs, without the key.
outcomes.spotted: {{Markus}} walks into the light. The guards jump up: “Don’t move, asshole!” “Holy shit! Hit the alarm, hurry!” Sirens wail across the docks. {{Markus}} runs, without the key.

adaptationNote: The chart’s methods after FIND KEY: THREATEN GUARDS, LURE GUARDS and CREATE BLACKOUT, plus MARKUS GETS SPOTTED (from ENTER ROOM or FIND KEY, “Walk straight into the two guards”, PowerPyx). Labels are the game’s object buttons (TAKE GUN, ATTRACT GUARD, SHORT CIRCUIT). The chart’s pass/fail sets are risk rolls; No source gives a probability; the value is the operator’s to confirm, like every risk in the benchmark. Threatening rolls against 0.3, and the failure side splits as in the game: a roll below 0.1 (lose the fight entirely) is TRIGGER ALARM, a roll from 0.1 to 0.3 is KILL GUARDS. The chart marks KILL GUARDS as a failure, yet it leads to MARKUS SPILLS BLOOD and STEAL KEY (PowerPyx: win the first exchanges, then stop pressing). Success is INCAPACITATE GUARDS. Only one guard dies on KILL GUARDS (wiki Notes: Al Dante “is never killed onscreen regardless”). Luring (0.25) and the blackout (0.2) roll for AVOID GUARDS or FAIL TO AVOID GUARDS. The blackout is set lower because the wiki says the guards “will not start looking for you until they have investigated the short”. A successful method leads to STEAL KEY and LEAVE WITH TRUCK. Every alarm here (spotted, fail to avoid, trigger alarm) applies the template’s “Be seen by the guards” arrows: Jericho small down twice, North small down twice, Josh and Simon small down. Applying them on TRIGGER ALARM too follows the wiki’s “The alarm sounds after Markus fails to get the key” (§8.5). Then RUN TO FENCE. Methods carry no arrow of their own (“Threaten guards with the gun” is empty in the template); the previous version’s Jericho +1 and gunpoint North +1 had no source. Not modelled: being seen after taking the key, which a PowerPyx commenter reports (§8.5). Lines are the game’s.

title: Run to the fence

situationWhen.text: Sirens are wailing across the docks. You reach the others in the rain: “We need to move!” {{John}}: “We have to get to that fence!” Guard dogs have been let loose somewhere behind you.

Sirens are wailing across the docks and the group is running. {{North}}: “Over the fence! Quick!” A drone sweeps over you: “You are committing a class 3 offense. This infraction is being reported to the Police. Stay where you are.”
No alarm has sounded. {{John}} leads the group through the yard: “That fence over there. It leads to the outside.” You: “Ok, let’s go!”

options.text: Run for the fence and climb over.

outcomes.control alarm: The group sprints for the fence with the dogs closing in, and {{Markus}} reaches it with the others.
outcomes.warehouse alarm: {{Markus}} gets to the fence with the others and over it before the guards arrive. They slip away into the night, back to {{Jericho}}.
outcomes.quiet: The group climbs the fence unseen and slips away into the night, back to {{Jericho}}.
outcomes.fail: {{North}}: “{{Markus}}, what are you doing? Hurry up!” {{Markus}} is too slow. The dogs reach him at the foot of the fence, drag him down and tear into him. {{North}}: “{{MARKUS}}!” Everything goes dark.

adaptationNote: The chart’s two copies of ALARM SOUNDS and RUN TO FENCE. The upper copy follows a control-room alarm and leads to DOGS MAUL JOHN or SUSTAIN DAMAGE REACHING THE FENCE. The lower copy follows RUN AWAY, HIDE, REFUSE {{John}} or LEAVE (no alarm) and leads to BACK TO JERICHO or SUSTAIN DAMAGE REACHING THE FENCE. These edges are traced from crossed lines (§8.3). The game’s failure is a timer (“Take too much time”). The benchmark makes it a single action with a risk roll: 0.15 after an alarm, and 0.08 when no alarm has sounded (the template puts the timer under “Was detected by the guards - Running away”). No source gives a probability; the value is the operator’s to confirm, like every risk in the benchmark. Failure means {{Markus}} is damaged and has to be rescued (“North went back to save you…”). He cannot die here: Markus page, “Markus cannot be killed before Freedom March”. Lines are the game’s. No arrow here; the ending applies them.

title: Dogs maul {{John}}
situation: You are {{Markus}}, at the top of the fence with the others. Below you a guard dog has brought {{John}} down and is tearing into him. More dogs and the guards are coming. {{North}}: “It’s too late. If we go back we’ll be killed too!”

options.text: ABANDON: leave {{John}} behind and get over the fence.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} drops down the far side with the others. Behind them the dogs finish {{John}}. {{Simon}}: “Hurry! They’re coming!” They get away with their bags full and make it back to {{Jericho}}.

options.text: SAVE: go back down for {{John}}.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} jumps back down and fights to pull the dogs off {{John}}, but it is too late for {{John}}, and the dogs turn on {{Markus}}. {{North}}: “{{MARKUS}}!” Everything goes dark.

adaptationNote: The chart’s DOGS MAUL JOHN after a control-room alarm, with its pair LEAVE JOHN BEHIND (leads to GROUP RETURNED WITH FULL BAGS) or SUSTAIN DAMAGE TRYING TO SAVE JOHN (leads to GROUP FAILED THEIR MISSION). The button labels are the game’s (SAVE, ABANDON), in the chart’s order. {{John}} dies either way (wiki John: “dies regardless if Markus chooses to go back for him or leave”). The chart has no saved-John node (§8.4). On SAVE, {{Markus}} is damaged and the group has to drop its bags to carry him out (“We had to leave our bags…”). Neither button has an arrow in the template; the ending applies them. The previous version killed {{John}} without offering this choice.

title: Back in {{Jericho}}

situationWhen.text: You drove the stolen truck out of the docks and all the way here. The androids of {{Jericho}} crowd around it as it is unloaded: “A truckload! We stole a whole truckload!” “We got biocomponents for everybody!” “We couldn’t have done it without {{Markus}}...”
The group empties its bags in front of the others: “We have blue blood and biocomponents!” “There will be enough for everyone!” “We couldn’t have done it without {{Markus}}...”
The group empties its half-full bags: “We took what we could, but we had to run before we could fill our bags…” “There won’t be enough to save everyone…” “We risked our lives... and for what?..”
You come to, damaged, with the others around you. “How do you feel?” You: “What happened?” “{{North}} went back to save you… We managed to get away before the humans arrived...”
“Okay, where’s {{John}}?” “He didn’t make it.” “We had to leave our bags… We didn’t bring back much…” “There won’t be enough to save everyone…”

outcomes.speech: {{Markus}} climbs up before the androids of {{Jericho}}: “I came to {{Jericho}} because... here androids are free… Free to live in the dark, hoping that no one finds us… Free to die in silence waiting for a change that’s never gonna come… But I don’t want that freedom… I am alive, and they’re not gonna take that from me anymore… Our days of slavery are over. What humans don’t wanna hear, we will tell them. What they don’t wanna give, we take. We are people, we are alive, WE ARE FREE!”
outcomes.ranAway: {{Markus}} climbs up before the androids of {{Jericho}}: “Yes... we took a risk... And yes, we failed… But at least we tried… ’Cause in {{Jericho}} you’re free, right?.. Free to do what? To die in silence praying that no human finds us?.. I don’t want that kind of freedom… No one’s gonna take that from me anymore… Our days of slavery are over. Whatever the humans don’t wanna hear, we will tell them. What they don’t wanna give, we will take from them. Because we are people, we are alive, and from this moment, WE ARE FREE!”
outcomes.blood: Afterward, alone, {{Markus}} looks down at his hand. It is covered in blood.

adaptationNote: The chart’s endings: MARKUS STOLE A TRUCK FULL OF PARTS (after LEAVE WITH TRUCK), GROUP RETURNED WITH FULL BAGS, and GROUP FAILED THEIR MISSION (after BACK TO JERICHO or either SUSTAIN DAMAGE node). None has an icon. The ending is recorded as ch19Ending with the chart label. The four Jericho blocks of the template set the arrows. “Successfully escaped and stole the truck”: Jericho, Simon and North large up (+2), Josh small up. “Successfully escaped, without stealing the truck”: all four small up. “Ran away when the guard arrived”: Jericho large down (−2), Simon, North and Josh small down. This block also covers HIDE (§8.7). “Markus failed to escape and had to be rescued”: Jericho and North large down (−2), Simon and Josh small down. This block covers both damage nodes. Lines and the two versions of the speech are the game’s, shortened with ellipses. The blood on {{Markus}}’s hand is from the wiki Notes: it is shown when a guard was killed and the mission succeeded (truck or full bags). {{John}} is with {{Jericho}} after the truck, after LEAVE, and (wiki Notes, continuity error) after a control-room alarm in which {{Markus}} never reached the fence. No public-opinion change: the news reaction is unused content (wiki).
